# Administrator

You'll be joining a supportive team where your organisational skills, attention to detail and contribution will make a real difference to the day-to-day success of the business.

title: Executive Assistant
description:
Executive Assistant

Location: Sheffield (Primarily Office-Based with up to 1 Day Hybrid Working)
Salary: £40,000 £50,000 FTE (Dependent on Experience)
Hours: Full Time (Flexibility Available for the Right Candidate)
Contract Type: Permanent

The Opportunity

We're delighted to be supporting our client in the search for an experienced and highly organised Executive Assistant to support the MD of a fantastic global company.

This is a rare opportunity to become a trusted partner to the company's MD, helping them maximise their impact by managing priorities, protecting their time, and ensuring the smooth running of day-to-day operations. Working at the heart of the business, you'll support senior leadership, complex diary management, international travel arrangements over different time zones,codordinate key projects and events, and play an important role in helping the organisation continue its impressive growth journey.

If you're a proactive problem-solver who thrives in a fast-paced environment and enjoys bringing structure and organisation to busy schedules, we'd love to hear from you.

Key Responsibilities
- Provide comprehensive executive support to the MD, managing priorities across multiple business areas.
- Proactively manage complex diaries, International travel plans,schedules, meetings, and appointments and monitor and triage inboxes, responding on behalf of the MD where appropriate.
- Monitor and triage inboxes, responding on behalf of senior leaders where appropriate.
- Arrange travel, accommodation, and detailed itineraries.
- Prepare meeting agendas, papers, briefing notes, and follow-up actions.
- Manage actions arising from meetings, ensuring tasks are followed through to completion.
- Coordinate leadership meetings, strategy sessions.
- Liaise confidently with clients, colleagues, and external stakeholders and handle confidential and sensitive information with the highest level of professionalism and discretion.
- Handle confidential and sensitive information with the highest level of professionalism and discretion.

What We're Looking For
- Proven experience as an Executive Assistant supporting senior leaders, directors, or business owners with experience supporting multiple stakeholders simultaneously.
- Exceptional organisational and time-management skills.
- Strong communication skills, both written and verbal with excellent attention to detail.
- Confident using Microsoft 365, Teams, Outlook, and modern workplace technology.
- Professional, diplomatic, and capable of dealing with confidential information.
- Experience handling complex diary management and international travel plans across many time zones.

What's In It For You?
- Competitive salary of £40,000 £50,000 FTE, depending on experience.
- Pension scheme
- Up to one day per week working from home.
- 25 days holiday plus bank holidays
- Modern Sheffield office with parking options available.
- Comprehensive personal development.

Our Commitment to Inclusion

The Talent Division is committed to creating an inclusive recruitment process where everyone feels valued, respected, and able to succeed.

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe diverse teams make stronger businesses and encourage applications from all suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, gender identity, marriage or civil partnership status, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation.

If you require any adjustments during the recruitment process, please let us know and we'll be happy to support you.

title: Insolvency Administrator
description:
Insolvency Administrator
Doncaster or Sheffield £25,000 £28,000 DOE Full-time, office-based

An established independent insolvency practice in South Yorkshire is adding two Insolvency Administrators, one to its Doncaster team and one to its Sheffield team.

This is a close-knit firm of around 25 people handling cases a year. The work is mainly CVLs, and the firm is increasingly winning more complex appointments, including administrations. You'll run a varied caseload with direct access to the IPs and Directors, which is rare at a larger firm.

What you'll do:
- Manage a varied caseload across corporate and personal insolvency procedures
- Prepare statutory reports, notices and correspondence to regulatory deadlines
- Support investigations into company conduct and asset realisations
- Reconcile case bank accounts and keep case files accurate and audit-ready
- Deal with creditors, directors, debtors, banks and legal representatives
- Spot risks early and escalate issues to keep cases compliant

What they're looking for:
- Insolvency experience, ideally around 2 years
- Strong attention to detail and confidence with numbers and reconciliations
- Good Excel skills, with experience of IPS an advantage
- Any exposure to administrations is a bonus
- Organised and proactive, and comfortable handling sensitive queries

Why apply
- A salary of up to £30k depending on experience
- A small team where your work gets noticed
- Clear room to progress as the firm takes on more complex work

Apply now or contact Joel at ECS Recruitment for a confidential conversation.

title: Reablement Care Coordinator
description:
Belmont Recruitment are currently looking for an experienced Adult Social Care Practitioner to join Sheffield City Council's Reablement Team on an initial 6 month temporary contract. This is a full-time role working 37 hours per week, Monday to Friday.

You will be responsible for assessing the needs of adults requiring social care support, developing individual care and support plans, and completing reviews to promote independence, wellbeing and positive outcomes. You will work collaboratively with individuals, carers, health professionals and community organisations, ensuring support is delivered in line with the Care Act 2014.

Key Responsibilities
- Complete Care Act 2014 assessments to identify eligible care and support needs.
- Develop person-centred care and support plans in partnership with individuals and their carers.
- Conduct reviews of care and support arrangements, ensuring needs are being met effectively.
- Carry out risk assessments and identify appropriate measures to reduce risks.
- Promote independence, choice, recovery and wellbeing through a strengths-based approach.
- Identify and respond to safeguarding concerns, following relevant policies and procedures.
- Provide information, advice and signposting to housing, welfare benefits and other relevant support services.
- Undertake home visits across Sheffield to assess needs and provide support.

Requirements
- NVQ Level 3 or equivalent relevant qualification, or the ability to demonstrate competence at this level.
- Experience working with adults with physical disabilities, mental health conditions or other social care needs.
- Knowledge of the Care Act 2014, Mental Capacity Act 2005 and safeguarding procedures.
- Experience completing assessments, care planning and risk assessments.

Please apply with an up to date CV ASAP if this role would be of interest to you!

description: About the Role We are looking for a friendly, professional, and reliable Receptionist to join our busy GP practice on a permanentbasis. As the first point of contact for patients, you will play a key role in ensuring a smooth and welcoming experience for everyone visiting or contacting the practice. Key Responsibilities Greeting patients and visitors in a courteous and efficient manner Managing appointments, telephone queries, and repeat prescriptions Handling patient information confidentially and accurately using our clinical system e.g. SystmOne Supporting the clinical team with administrative tasks Working collaboratively with colleagues to deliver excellent patient care Maintaining a calm, professional approach at all times What Were Looking For Experience in a receptionist or administrative role (GP practice/NHS preferred but not essential) Excellent communication and customer service skills Strong IT skills and attention to detail Ability to multitask and remain composed under pressure A positive, flexible attitude and a commitment to teamwork Respect for patient confidentiality and data protection protocols Greet patients and visitors in a courteous and professional manner. Manage incoming telephone calls and respond to patient enquiries. Book, amend and cancel appointments using the clinical system. Signpost patients to the most appropriate healthcare professional or service. Process patient check-ins and arrivals. Handle requests for home visits in accordance with practice procedures. Register new patients and maintain accurate patient records. Process repeat prescription requests according to practice protocols. Scan, file and distribute incoming documentation. Manage incoming and outgoing correspondence, including emails and letters. Support clinicians with administrative tasks as required. Ensure all patient information is handled confidentially and in line with GDPR requirements. Provide excellent customer service to patients, carers and visitors. Deal with challenging situations calmly and professionally. Assist patients with online services and registration where appropriate. Promote practice services and health campaigns. Maintain confidentiality regarding patient, staff and practice information. Adhere to all practice policies, procedures and information governance standards. Complete mandatory training as required. Work collaboratively as part of the wider practice team. Participate in team meetings and training sessions. Undertake any reasonable duties appropriate to the role. Support colleagues during periods of absence or increased workload.

title: Reception Administrator
description: This role is at the heart of our organisations day-to-day operations. As the first point of contact for many of our clients, visitors, and team members, youll play a vital part in creating a welcoming, professional, and efficient environment. We created this role to support our growing need for reliable, organised, and people-focused administrative support. Youll be joining a team that values collaboration, empowerment, attention to detail, and a proactive approach to problem-solving. Your work will help ensure that our front-of-house experience reflects the high standards we set across all our services. From managing enquiries and coordinating appointments to supporting internal processes, youll be instrumental in keeping things running smoothly and helping others do their best work. We provide the tools and support individuals need to challenge themselves and push their recovery to its fullest potential, empowering them not only to recover but to thrive. As a Reception Administrator at STEPS, you will provide the first point of contact for STEPS clients, visitors, external organisations and suppliers as well as providing vital administrative support for our service. You will work as part of a wider inter-disciplinary team with collective responsibility for delivering first-class service in rehabilitative care aligned with STEPS values and behaviours. We know that exceptional care begins with exceptional people. Thats why weve built a specialist interdisciplinary team, who bring not only skill and experience, but real compassion to every interaction. We employ 180+ team members in both clinical positions and in business support roles and we are proud of the culture we have established where all team members share our philosophy, values and dedication to delivering excellent client care. Our team is united by a common purpose, dedicated to continually learning from one another, and committed to giving their utmost for those we support. We invest and nurture the development of our team, and through training, shared learning, and research, we give them the tools to grow, stay inspired, and remain at the forefront of their area of work. This Job description is an outline which reflects the present requirements of the post and is not intended to be exhaustive list of duties the post holder will be expected to fulfil. To provide a professional, courteous and prompt first point of contact for clients, visiting families, guests and external visitors. To be responsible for providing a client-centred reception service which; - Deals with all enquiries appropriately, referring issues which cannot be resolved immediately by referring to the correct team member - Maintains appropriate call and action logs - Ensures that the correct processes are followed for client and guest sign in and sign out, including making sure people are aware of the correct site safety procedures - Carries out all start and end of day processes for reception - Ensures that the reception area and the admin office is kept tidy and presentable at all times - Takes delivery and sign for packages and post - Takes cash/card payments from clients and team members when necessary - Books taxis for clients and visitors when requested or agreed by a STEPS team member according to the relevant procedures To provide additional administrative support as appropriate, for example; - Typing up clinical notes as required - Input client timetables - Raise Invoices - Order clinical supplies, stationery and other equipment as requested To comply with STEPS policies and procedures at all times To maintain client confidentiality at all times whilst carrying out duties. To ensure confidentiality of information in respect of records maintained and tasks undertaken To undertake any other duties which may be specified from time to time by Head of Admin that are within the level and responsibility appropriate to the post To effectively communicate using a variety of styles that demonstrates the values and behaviours of STEPS. To communicate with people clearly and in a manner and at a level and pace appropriate to their abilities, preferences and beliefs. To be respectful of a clients dignity at all times and develop effective relationships with clients, their families, carers, the interdisciplinary team.
